description: We seek permission to remove tree T, identified as a False Acacia (Robinia pseudoacacia).This tree is not visible from any publicly accessible location and therefore offers no visual amenity to the wider area. Additionally, False Acacia is not a species well suited for long-term retention within small residential gardens due to its growth habit and invasive tendencies.While not a requirement under Section 211, we propose to plant a native Hawthorn as a replacement. This species will provide greater ecosystem benefits over time and is more appropriate for the setting.It is also important to note that neighbours have previously raised formal concerns regarding tree T. They stated that on the night of 12?13 September 2017, a large False Acacia?likely the parent tree of T?fell and caused damage to nearby properties at 72 Kilravock Street. This incident was attended by a Westminster arboricultural officer. - Residents have since observed that T appears to have propagated from the original tree via root suckers, a known and problematic trait of this species. False Acacias are often considered invasive or undesirable in domestic gardens due to their vigorous root systems and potential for uncontrolled spread. It is also likely that tree T was not intentionally planted but has nonetheless reached a considerable size.For these reasons, we believe removal and replacement with a more appropriate native species is both reasonable and responsible both for the enjoyment of our garden, for our neighbours and for the ecosystem.
